_meta.indication: Treatment of anemia associated with chronic renal failure (CRF) in adults, including patients on dialysis and not on dialysis; not indicated for anemia due to cancer chemotherapy

pivotal_trials.trial_name: BA16736 (Phase III anemia correction study, dialysis patients)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, multicenter, parallel-group correction study of IV Mircera 0.4 µg/kg every 2 weeks vs IV epoetin 3 times weekly (3:1 randomization)
pivotal_trials.population: On-dialysis patients with anemia associated with chronic kidney disease, not previously treated with epoetin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Hemoglobin response: increase in Hb ≥ 1.0 g/dL from baseline and a single Hb ≥ 11 g/dL without RBC transfusion before response, during the 24 weeks after first dose
pivotal_trials.result: Hemoglobin response rate 93.3% (95% CI: 87.7%, 96.9%) for Mircera vs 91.3% (95% CI: 79.2%, 97.6%) for epoetin

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of Mircera for the Treatment of Anemia in Dialysis Patients

pivotal_trials.trial_name: BA16738 (Phase III anemia correction study, non-dialysis patients)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, darbepoetin alfa-controlled, parallel-group study; patients randomized 1:1 to SC Mircera once every 2 weeks (0.6 µg/kg) vs SC darbepoetin alfa once weekly (0.45 µg/kg)
pivotal_trials.population: Non-dialysis patients with anemia associated with chronic kidney disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: (1) hemoglobin response rate (Hb increase ≥ 1.0 g/dL and reaching ≥ 11.0 g/dL) and (2) change in Hb concentration between baseline and evaluation periods (non-inferiority to darbepoetin, margin -0.75 g/dL)
pivotal_trials.result: Hemoglobin response rate 97.5% (95% CI: 93.8%, 99.3%) for Mircera vs 96.3% (95% CI: 92.1%, 98.6%) for darbepoetin alfa

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of Mircera in the Treatment of Anemia in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Not on Dialysis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥ 5%) are hypertension, diarrhea, nasopharyngitis, headache, and upper respiratory tract infection. Boxed warning for increased mortality and serious cardiovascular/thromboembolic events when ESAs are dosed to higher hemoglobin targets.
target_moa: Erythropoietin receptor activator (ESA) with greater in vivo activity and increased half-life vs erythropoietin; stimulates erythroid progenitor cells to increase red cell production, correcting the erythropoietin-deficiency anemia of CRF
modality: Pegylated protein (PEGylated epoetin beta) – methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta, a continuous erythropoietin receptor activator

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning: Increased mortality, serious cardiovascular and thromboembolic events, and tumor progression. In chronic renal failure, greater risks of death and serious cardiovascular events occurred when ESAs targeted higher versus lower hemoglobin (13.5 vs 11.3 g/dL; 14 vs 10 g/dL); individualize dosing to maintain Hb 10–12 g/dL.

rems.type: No REMS in the original approval; FDA required distribution of a Medication Guide under 21 CFR Part 208 (patient labeling), not a REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee for review; ESA safety was discussed at a joint Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs/Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee meeting on September 11, 2007, but not specifically for this product.

description.text: Added new indication for IV Mircera for anemia associated with CKD in pediatric patients 5-17 years on hemodialysis converting from another ESA

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new indication for Mircera administered by intravenous route for the treatment of anemia associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD) in pediatric patients 5 to 17 years of age on hemodialysis who are converting from another erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) after their hemoglobin level was stabilized with an ESA.

description.text: Added subcutaneous once-monthly administration for correction of anemia in non-dialysis chronic kidney disease patients

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for the "Dosage and Administration" of the prescribing information to indicate that methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta can be administered by subcutaneous injection once a month for the correction of anemia in chronic kidney disease patients who are not on dialysis.

description.text: Expanded pediatric CKD anemia indication to patients 3 months to 17 years, on and not on dialysis, converting from another ESA, and added subcutaneous route of administration

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for extension of the indication for the treatment of anemia associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD) in pediatric patients 3 months to 17 years of age on dialysis and not on dialysis who are converting from another erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) after their hemoglobin level was stabilized with an ESA. Previously, the indication was approved for pediatric patients 5 to 17 years of age with CKD on hemodialysis. Additionally, this Prior Approval sBLA provides for a subcutaneous route of administration for pediatric patients. Previously, the pediatric patients could only use the intravenous route of administration.

basis.text: The clinical review records a Priority Designation for this BLA (STN 125164).

summary.text: Mircera (methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta) was a traditional BLA approval for anemia associated with chronic renal failure, approved November 14, 2007 on a second review cycle following a Complete Review Letter dated May 18, 2007. It was not an accelerated approval and carried no orphan, breakthrough, fast track, or RMAT designations; the clinical review notes a Priority Designation.

requirement.text: Phase 4 randomized, controlled, open-label, multicenter parallel-group study assessing all-cause mortality and cardiovascular morbidity in anemic CKD patients on and not on dialysis across a broad range of C-reactive protein concentrations, comparing methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta with another ESA.

citations.quote: 3. To conduct a phase 4, randomized, controlled, open label, multicenter parallel group study to assess the all cause mortality and cardiovascular morbidity in anemic patients with chronic kidney disease who are on dialysis and not undergoing dialysis. The study will enroll patients with a broad range of C-reactive protein blood concentrations and will randomize patients to treatment with either methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta or another erythropoiesis-stimulating agent.
